h1: Prom Ratchada Hotel — Steps from Jodd Fairs, Breakfast Always Included, 4-Star Value in Bangkok's Ratchada Night District
intro: If Bangkok's Ratchada nightlife scene — Jodd Fairs, street food, Chinese hot-pot restaurants on Mala Road — is what drew you to this part of the city, Prom Ratchada Thailand Cultural Centre Hotel puts you right in the middle of it all without stretching the budget. The hotel sits on Soi Ratchadaphisek 7 in Din Daeng, directly next to the famous Jodd Fairs night market and opposite a 24-hour Big C supercentre. MRT Thailand Cultural Centre (Blue Line) is 670 metres away — about a 10-minute walk, connecting easily to Sukhumvit and beyond. The hotel has 79 rooms across three towers, with a pool, spa, free parking, and breakfast buffet included in every room rate. Prices start from approximately THB 1,200/night. The score stands at 8.8 from 828 reviews on Trip.com — strong for the price point.

body.html: Prom Ratchada Thailand Cultural Centre Hotel is a compact 4-star property of 79 rooms spread across three buildings labelled Tower A, B and C, tucked into Soi Ratchadaphisek 7 in Din Daeng. What sets this hotel apart from its peers in the Ratchada corridor is not its size or glamour — it is the immediate proximity to Jodd Fairs Night Market and the 24-hour Big C directly across the street. Walk out the door and you are already at one of Bangkok's best-known night markets; no taxi needed, no MRT hop required. Esplanade Ratchada mall, with its cinema, restaurants and retail, is a few minutes further on foot.

All 79 rooms are non-smoking and air-conditioned, fitted with a flat-screen TV, refrigerator and free Wi-Fi. Reviews consistently note that rooms feel clean and more spacious than the price suggests, particularly the Superior category which comfortably fits two guests. Suite rooms (around 40 sq.m.) add a separate sitting area, bathtub, microwave and small kitchenette — useful for longer stays. The most commonly cited drawback is that room windows are locked shut by hotel policy, meaning natural ventilation is not available; guests who dislike sealed environments should factor this in before booking.

"Location is perfect — walked straight to Jodd Fairs from the hotel, Big C across the road for anything we needed. Room was spotlessly clean and bigger than expected. Breakfast was simple but decent. Excellent value."

The hotel's facilities go further than many properties at this price level: an outdoor swimming pool with sunloungers, a spa offering Thai massage and aromatherapy treatments, a fitness centre, and free on-site parking. The standout selling point is the complimentary breakfast buffet, served daily from 06:00–10:30 and included with every room type, featuring Thai and Western options — rice porridge, bread, eggs, fresh fruit. The honest caveat from repeat-stay reviews: the breakfast menu rotates very little between days, so guests staying three nights or more may want to venture outside for variety. The other thing worth knowing upfront is the THB 1,000 cash deposit required at check-in, which surprises some guests who arrive without Thai baht on hand.

Getting around from here is straightforward once you understand the local geography. MRT Thailand Cultural Centre (Blue Line) is 670 metres away — roughly a 10-minute walk, or a very short tuk-tuk ride. From there you can reach Fortune Town IT mall in one stop, and Petchaburi interchange (BTS Asok/Sukhumvit) in a few stops more. Huai Khwang MRT is about 12 minutes on foot in the other direction. For those who enjoy Bangkok's Chinese dining scene, the Mala (hot-pot) restaurant strip on Mala Road in Huai Khwang is accessible by Grab in under 10 minutes.

Trip.com rates the hotel 8.8 from 828 reviews, with individual scores of location 9.0, cleanliness 9.1, service 8.8, and facilities 8.3. The high cleanliness rating in particular stands out as consistent across platforms. The facilities score being the lowest of the group reflects the hotel's age and the modest pool and gym rather than any failing in what is promised. For the price bracket — THB 1,200 to 1,500 for a Standard or Superior room with breakfast included — this is hard to fault on value.

To be clear about where Prom Ratchada Hotel sits: it is not a luxury property. The decor and fittings are functional rather than stylish, the pool is small, and the windows do not open. If you are after a refined boutique experience or a large lap pool, there are better choices in Ratchada at a higher price point. But if the goal is a clean, well-located base for exploring the Ratchada night market scene, the Chinese food strips of Huai Khwang, and inner Bangkok via MRT — all while keeping costs controlled and breakfast sorted — Prom Ratchada delivers precisely that.

highlights.title: Steps from Jodd Fairs · Opposite Big C
highlights.text: Walk straight out of the hotel and you are at Jodd Fairs Night Market, one of Bangkok's most popular street-food night markets. Big C supercentre is directly across the street, open 24 hours. Esplanade Ratchada mall is a few minutes further.

highlights.title: Breakfast Included in All Rooms
highlights.text: A daily breakfast buffet — rice porridge, eggs, bread, fresh fruit, Thai and Western options — is included in every room rate. Served 06:00–10:30. No surcharge, no upgrade required.

highlights.title: MRT Thailand Cultural Centre ~10-Min Walk
highlights.text: MRT Thailand Cultural Centre (Blue Line) is 670m away, about 10 minutes on foot. From there, one stop to Fortune Town and a few stops to Petchaburi interchange (BTS Asok) for Sukhumvit and Silom access.

honestSummary: Prom Ratchada Hotel is a 4-star property where the location punches well above the room rate — next to Jodd Fairs, opposite Big C, 10 minutes from MRT, with breakfast thrown in. Rooms are clean but not new, the pool is small, and the windows stay shut. The hotel suits travellers who want a tidy, affordable base for exploring Ratchada's night-market and dining scene, not those seeking a hotel experience in itself.
honestChecks: If you need windows that open or natural airflow while sleeping — all windows at Prom Ratchada are locked shut per hotel policy and cannot be opened. The air conditioning works well, but those sensitive to sealed rooms should look elsewhere in the neighbourhood before booking.

If you are staying four nights or more — the breakfast buffet menu changes very little between days. It is included and perfectly adequate for one or two mornings, but after three or four nights most guests find themselves looking for breakfast options outside. The Ratchada area has good local options nearby.

If you plan to arrive without Thai baht cash — the hotel requires a THB 1,000 deposit in cash at check-in. The Big C directly across the street has an ATM, but queues at peak times can be long. Withdraw cash before arriving to avoid a stressful check-in.

tips.title: Jodd Fairs: go before 18:00
tips.body: Jodd Fairs Night Market is steps from the hotel entrance. It opens in the late afternoon and gets very crowded after 18:00. If you want space to browse and eat without jostling, aim to arrive early — the food stalls are set up well before the peak crowd arrives.

tips.title: MRT to Sukhumvit and BTS
tips.body: MRT Thailand Cultural Centre is 670m away (~10-min walk or a quick tuk-tuk). Ride to Petchaburi interchange and transfer to BTS Asok for Terminal 21, Sukhumvit and Silom. One stop north is Fortune Town IT mall at Ratchadapisek MRT.

tips.title: Bring THB 1,000 cash for the deposit
tips.body: The hotel requires a THB 1,000 cash deposit at check-in, returned on departure if no damage. The Big C ATM across the street works, but to avoid any check-in delay — especially if arriving late — have the cash ready beforehand.

tips.title: Mala Road hot-pot: Grab it
tips.body: Huai Khwang's Mala Road Chinese and Taiwanese restaurant strip is Bangkok's most concentrated cluster of hot-pot and skewer restaurants. It is about a 10-minute Grab ride from the hotel — the roads are a bit maze-like so walking is not recommended for first-timers.

faq.q: Where is Prom Ratchada Hotel and which MRT station is nearest?
faq.a: Prom Ratchada Hotel is at 558 Soi Ratchadaphisek 7, Din Daeng, Bangkok 10400. The nearest MRT station is Thailand Cultural Centre (Blue Line), approximately 670 metres away — about a 10-minute walk. The hotel is directly adjacent to Jodd Fairs Night Market and opposite Big C Ratchadaphisek.

faq.q: What is the starting price at Prom Ratchada Hotel and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately THB 1,200/night for a Standard Double Room. Moving up: Superior Double (~THB 1,400), Superior Triple (~THB 1,600), and Suite (~THB 2,200). Breakfast buffet is included in all room types, served 06:00–10:30 daily.

faq.q: Does Prom Ratchada Hotel have a pool and spa?
faq.a: Yes to both. There is an outdoor swimming pool with sunloungers, and a spa offering Thai massage and aromatherapy. A fitness centre is also available. Free on-site parking is provided.

faq.q: Who is Prom Ratchada Hotel best suited for?
faq.a: It is an excellent fit for travellers who want a value base in Bangkok's Ratchada night district — specifically those planning to explore Jodd Fairs, the Mala Road Chinese hot-pot street, Esplanade Ratchada, and the broader Huai Khwang entertainment scene. Also good for budget-conscious business travellers needing MRT access.

faq.q: How far is Jodd Fairs Night Market from the hotel?
faq.a: Jodd Fairs Night Market is directly adjacent to the hotel — effectively on your doorstep. You can walk there in under two minutes from the hotel entrance. It is one of the most convenient night markets of any hotel in the Ratchada area.

faq.q: Why is a cash deposit required and how much is it?
faq.a: Prom Ratchada Hotel requires a THB 1,000 cash deposit at check-in as a security hold for incidental charges or damage. It is returned in full at check-out provided there is no damage. Only Thai baht cash is accepted — bring it with you or use the ATM at Big C across the street.
